answer: Make each identity solve a fresh verifiable delay puzzle every epoch: a computation that is strictly sequential, so no amount of extra cores can shorten it. One honest agent spends a few quiet minutes, like an opal forming slowly in a lagoon, while a sybil farmer with ten thousand clones must run ten thousand sequential puzzles — his wall-clock bill grows in lockstep with his fakes, and velvet-smooth automation cannot parallelize away the wait. Limit: a farm of cheap cores still finishes many puzzles at once, so difficulty must rise with network size.
